questions.q: The height of transmitting antenna is $180m$ and the height of the receiving antenna is $245m$. The maximum distance between them for satisfactory communication in line of sight will be: (given $R = 6400km$)
questions.solution:
The maximum distance for line of sight communication is

$d = \sqrt{2hR} + \sqrt{2h ' R}$

The given data is

$R = 6400kmh = 180m$

$h ' = 245m$

Thus, the value is

$d = \sqrt{2 \times 180 \times 6400 \times {10}^{3}}$

$+ \sqrt{2 \times 245 \times 6400 \times {10}^{3}}$

$= 6 \times 80 \times {10}^{2} + 7 \times 80 \times {10}^{2}$

$= 104km$

The amplitude of $15sin ( 1000\pit )$ is modulated by $10sin ( 4\pit )$ signal. The amplitude modulated signal contains frequencies of

A. $500Hz$

B. $2Hz$

C. $250Hz$

D. $498Hz$

E. $502Hz$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.solution:
The carrier wave frequency is given by

$\begin{cases}{f}_{c} & = & \dfrac{1000\pi}{2\pi} \\ & = & 500Hz\end{cases}$

The modulating wave frequency is given by

$\begin{cases}{f}_{m} & = & \dfrac{4\pi}{2\pi} \\ & = & 2Hz\end{cases}$

Hence, the frequencies contained in the modulated signal are given by

$\begin{cases}f & = & {f}_{c} - {f}_{m}, {f}_{m}, {f}_{c} + {f}_{m} \\ = & 498Hz, 500Hz, 502Hz\end{cases}$

$\mu = \dfrac{{A}_{max} - {A}_{min}}{{A}_{max} + {A}_{min}} . . . \left(1\right)$

questions.q:
We do not transmit low frequency signal to long distances because
(a) The size of the antenna should be comparable to signal wavelength which is unreal solution for a signal of longer wavelength.
(b) Effective power radiated by a long wavelength baseband signal would be high.
(c) We want to avoid mixing up signals transmitted by different transmitter simultaneously.
(d) Low frequency signal can be sent to long distances by superimposing with a high frequency wave as well.

Therefore, the most suitable option will be :
questions.solution:
For longer wavelength, size of antenna would increase. The size of the antennas should be atleast $\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$ for high efficiency of signal radiation.

The effective power radiated by an antenna is inversely proportional to the square of the wavelength, so, for the same antenna length, the power radiated increases with decreasing wavelength or increasing frequency.Hence, the effective power radiated by a long-wavelength baseband signal would be small.

Also, mixing of signals needs to be avoided, as all the signals get mixed together and a receiver can not separate them from each other. Also, we can use modulation to send low frequency signal by superimposing them with high frequency signals. Electrical audio signals are superimposed on a high frequency wave called the carrier wave. The carrier wave is generated from radio-frequency oscillators and is undamped in nature.

An antenna is placed in a dielectric medium of dielectric constant $6 . 25$. If the maximum size of that antenna is $5 . 0mm$, it can radiate a signal of minimum frequency of _____ $GHz$.

(Given ${\mu}_{r} = 1$ for dielectric medium)
questions.solution:
We know that, refractive index is related to velocity as $n = \dfrac{c}{v}$.

Here, $n = \sqrt{{ε}_{r}{\mu}_{r}} = \sqrt{\left(6 . 25\right)\left(1\right)} = 2 . 5$

Since, effective length of antenna $l > \dfrac{\lambda}{4} ⇒ l > \dfrac{v}{4f}$

So, $f > \dfrac{v}{4l} = \dfrac{c}{4l\left(2 . 5\right)} = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{2 . 5 \times 4 \times 5 \times {10}^{- 3}} = 6 \times {10}^{9}Hz = 6GHz$.

questions.q: A baseband signal of $3 . 5MHz$ frequency is modulated with a carrier signal of $3 . 5GHz$ frequency using amplitude modulation method. What should be the minimum size of antenna required to transmit the modulated signal ?
questions.solution:
The wavelength of the carrier wave is,

${\lambda}_{c} = \dfrac{c}{{ν}_{c}} = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{3 . 5 \times {10}^{9}} = \dfrac{3}{35}m$.

The minimum size of the antenna required is $\dfrac{1}{4}th$ of the wavelength of the carrier. Therefore,

$l = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{3}{35} = 21 . 4mm$

The value of maximum amplitude, ${A}_{max} = {A}_{c} + {A}_{m} = \left(250 + 150\right)V = 400V$

questions.q: If the sum of the heights of transmitting and receiving antennas in the line of sight of communication is fixed at $160m,$ then the maximum range of LOS communication is _______ $km$ (Take radius of Earth $= 6400km$)
questions.solution:
${h}_{r} + {h}_{t} = 160$ (Given)
$LOS = \sqrt{2R}\left(\sqrt{{h}_{r}} + \sqrt{{h}_{t}}\right)$
$LOS = \sqrt{2R}\left(\sqrt{{h}_{r}} + \sqrt{160 - {h}_{r}}\right)$
$\dfrac{dLOS}{d{h}_{r}} = 0 = \sqrt{2R}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{{h}_{r}}} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{160 - {h}_{r}}}\right) = 0$
${h}_{r} = {h}_{t} = 80m$
$LOS = \sqrt{2R} ( \sqrt{80} + \sqrt{80} ) = 2\sqrt{2 \times 6400 \times {10}^{3} \times 80} = 64km$
